name: Richat Structure, Mauritania
clue: Concentric rings of exposed rock sit amid the desert.
explanation: The rings look like an impact crater from orbit. They’re layers of an uplifted dome that erosion exposed, with the tougher rock standing out as ridges.

name: Grand Canyon, Arizona
clue: A narrow river winds far below a snow-covered plateau.
explanation: The Colorado River cut down through the rock as it carried sediment away. Tributaries and erosion along the walls helped widen the canyon.
choices: A fault dropping a block of land

name: Malaspina Glacier (Sít’ Tlein), Alaska
clue: Dark bands fold and loop across a broad, pale lobe.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Jesse Allen, using USGS Landsat data
explanation: Ice spills from mountain valleys onto a plain and spreads outward. As the glacier surges and slows, it folds bands of rock debris into the loops visible from above.

name: Lake Natron, Tanzania
clue: Crimson shallows border pale salt deposits.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Joshua Stevens, using USGS Landsat data
explanation: As water evaporates from the shallow lake, dissolved salts become more concentrated and can form pale crusts. Salt-loving microorganisms give some of the remaining pools their red and pink colours.

name: Holuhraun lava field, Iceland
clue: A dark, lobed patch spreads across a lighter plain.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Jesse Allen, using NASA EO-1 ALI data
explanation: Lava poured from a fissure during the 2014 eruption and spread across the plain. As it cooled, it formed the dark rock and irregular edges of the new lava field.
